review:
The best ever concert I have watched (at that time). 
Don Juan by Strauss has the most catching beginning, also very suitable for the starting piece of the concert. From then on, it is added to my playlist.
No much impression on the Horn Concerto, as difficult (or contemporary) as Salonen's other works. I just feeling that horn is very difficult to play; the player needs to clean the liquid inside the instrument during the pauses; and there is a skill to clog the horn to change the timbre. And now I know Stefan Dohr may be one of the current best horn players; maybe the only horn player I know that will play as soloist in concerts. 
Sibelius No. 5 is often conducted by Salonen. During my 'preview' listening, I do not have a strong impression for the symphony (except the short piece of 'Swan Call'). But Salonen did make it. The performance left me the most memorable second movement (normally slow) even the whole symphony is rather slow. The struggling low-volumn strings before the swan call is clearly heard and make the moment of the swan call magnificent. The ending is also unusually astonishing: several pauses challenge those hotheaded audience.
Anyway, Salonen is my very anticipated conductor since then, although his composing works...

review:
I got the ticket of Lang Lang in the regular selling time: a miracle.
This is the first time to hear the work of Salonen. In fact, Castor is not that unintelligible. There is some touching movement bringing out the Greek mythical feeling. 
Grieg's piano concerto: it is my first time hear this composer. A Stunning beginning! and that is enough for me to add to my playlist. Lang Lang's body move is also so 'impressive' that I understand why he is sometimes criticized as greasy. While his body moves and rubato for this concerto is suitable, rendering the dramatic melody. The four-hand encore with Tarmo is also funny to watch. Such an encore also need preparation, I guess!
Lemminkainen Suite is relatively rarely performed as a whole suite. My rough feeling is that the music keeps struggling in a lowkey register. But it is not depressive; the lowkey register brings a cold, tragic atmosphere while the music is moving forward, as the hero surpasses the obstacles on his way. I will say this work is more exotic than other North Europe works (and Sibelius No.5 Symphony which I have heard).

'Spring': Fantastic. The performance let me listen to Schumann Symphony No. 1 more, as a daily music choice, which is my 5-star rating standard. The symphony itself is easy to understand like a tone poem. The performance is flawless (from my view) with impressive brass.

venue: Hong Kong Cultural Centre Grand Theatre
review:
A good chance and beginning to enjoy some operas. Cav/Pag is also not very long so I guess the operas are attractive enough to watch with some friends.
The costume design is good and classical, no special 'modern reinterpretation', very nice. Although the Sicilian coppola (flat cap) on Hong Kong local actors make them look like gangsters in the HK triads...
Cavalleria Rusticana: the story is simple; love and death. Santuzza is the best vocal. Intermezzo is too peaceful that makes audience forget the duel will start soon. Turiddu's performance is also dramatic enough as a pure 渣男; the only sympathy for him may be from his final begging: ask his mom to treat Santuzza well. 
Pagliacci: the plot is very well designed, but the Chinese soprano for Nedda is not as good as other singers: her voice cannot penetrate the hall and sound vague. The baritone for Alfio/Tonio contributes to two distinctive roles tonight, with both singing and acting vividly.
Btw, the music from HKPhil is also 'purer' (in a better sense) than the previous opera experience by the Czech orchestra.

review:
Most enthusiastic audience I have ever watched, aroused by the enthusiastic Flórez (with 5 encores!).
Vocal music can be more impressive than instruments. The starting two pieces are not really ear-catching, but from 'Una furtiva lagrima' all the pieces are great and perfect.
Spanish zarzuelas are interesting and easy to get ('Al mismito rey del moro').
Werther: Pourquoi me réveiller? is another best one. It is better singing with triste, not with the 'full-power' high voice (compared with the record of Bocelli).

I can also sense that the conductor Spotti have more 'operatic' details for the instruments. The overture of Cenerentola and Prelude of Macbeth are more dramatic, better than the records. A so great night that I clapped my hand to red.

The Sisters' Islands: the most interesting contemporary piece I have listened to. It goes with Malay and Chinese flavored melody. The music brings out very concrete pictures about the islandic resident life. 
Chloe: Fully expressional performance on the Mendelssohn violin concerto. Her violin solo can penetrate into the minds. Some details are not relaxing or easy compared to Heifetz's version, but that's too much for her now.
Mahler 1: In fact, I thought it is very obvious to understand, not like the stereotypical impression on Mahler's works. Some inharmonic sounds occur (maybe mistakes?) but the whole symphony is generally impressive. Maybe my expectation to Lintu and Singapore SO is higher.
Shenzhen Music Hall: the entrance time is too long. The hall is good (H area this time); the audience is tolerable.
